newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says to tighten insurance laws.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says to tighten insurance laws.

text.p: Insurance supervision in Singapore is to tighten with the end of self regulation for insurance and reinsurance brokers, Finance Minister Richard Hu told an industry conference on Tuesday.

Inaugurating the East Asian Insurance Congress conference in Singapore, Hu said the move to a more formal regulatory regime that would include licensing requirements for brokers would create "a more financially sound and professional insurance industry".

The laws to bring brokers into the regulatory scope of the Monetary Authority of Singapore are expected to be in place by 1998. They have been driven by the desire to protect policyholders' interests, Hu told conference delegates.
His comments about brokers followed remarks that regulators faced major changes in the industry as trade liberalisation gathered pace.
"Regulators need to be clear as to their role in a liberalised insurance market," he said.
